chapter: Los Angeles scene and the Ellington sound
title: Les Hite takes over and Hampton
summary: Hite and Hampton came west together; the band at first copied Ellington records because Western bands lagged Eastern ones.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Playing in Lionel Hampton's big band

blocks.x: Did Les Hite become leader when he joined, or came and was leader, or did he work in the band before he became leader?

No, he came -- he was leader when he came. And they -- at first they used to play a whole bunch of Ellington type arrangements. They used to copy off of records, plus the other numbers that they did, and that was a new trend too, this record copying business, because the eastern bands were definitely more advanced than the western bands in those days.
I don't think there was even a western style, hardly, in those early days. It was -- they all patterned after Fletcher Henderson, Ellington, Don Redman, and the different bands like that.
Did Lionel Hampton join the band with Les Hite?
Yes, Les and Lionel came out together,
and well, when the band finally got together, why Les and Lionel were in together.
And how big a band was that when Les was leader?
Let me see, three brass, three saxophones, it was about twelve pieces, ten or twelve pieces.
And that band there at the Cotton Club became the Les Hite band that was the -- continued as a steady band in Southern California, is that right?
Yes, it was one of the bands. By that time most all of the nightspots had bands of eight, ten, twelve pieces.
